# Blok — SPA (Inertia)

> Generated from docs/d/spa/**.mdx by `bun run docs:llms` — do not edit by hand.

Blok is a modular workflow platform. Its SPA layer speaks the Inertia v3
protocol against the stock `@inertiajs/react | vue3 | svelte` client: a page
is a workflow, a prop is a step (in any runtime), and the page contract is
declared once with `definePage()` outside the workflow callback so the
frontend can `import type` it.


---

# SPA (Inertia)

Source: /d/spa/index

Build a React, Vue or Svelte SPA on Blok — a page is a workflow, a prop is a step, navigation is the Inertia v3 protocol.

Blok speaks [Inertia.js **v3**](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/core-concepts/how-it-works).
You keep the stock `@inertiajs/react | vue3 | svelte` client — nothing is forked,
nothing is wrapped — and the server half is ordinary Blok:

- **a page is a workflow**, declared with `definePage()` and rendered by one
  `page` control step;
- **a prop is a step**, so any prop can run in any runtime (a Python node
  computing `stats` next to a TypeScript node listing `orders`);
- **navigation is the protocol**: the same URL answers an HTML shell on the
  first load and a JSON page object on an Inertia visit.

```ts src/workflows/dashboard.ts
import { defineNode, http, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { always, defer, definePage } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const currentUser = defineNode({
  name: "current-user",
  description: "The signed-in user.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ id: z.string(), email: z.string() }),
  execute: () => ({ id: "u-1", email: "ada@example.com" }),
});

const listOrders = defineNode({
  name: "list-orders",
  description: "Recent orders.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string(), total: z.number() })),
  execute: () => [{ id: "o-1", total: 120 }],
});

const heavyStats = defineNode({
  name: "heavy-stats",
  description: "Expensive dashboard aggregates.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ revenue: z.number() }),
  execute: () => ({ revenue: 42_000 }),
});

export const Dashboard = definePage("Dashboard", {
  auth: always(currentUser),
  orders: listOrders,
  stats: defer(heavyStats, { group: "dashboard" }),
});

export default workflow(
  "dashboard",
  { version: "1.0.0", trigger: http.get("/dashboard") },
  (req) => {
    Dashboard.render(req, "page", "/dashboard", { auth: {}, orders: {}, stats: {} });
  },
);
```

<Card title="Start here" icon="rocket" href="/d/spa/getting-started">
  Wire a Vite SPA to a Blok server and render your first page.
</Card>

## The protocol in one table

Everything the adapter reads and writes. The full field-by-field reference is
[The protocol](/d/spa/the-protocol).

| Direction | Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| → request | `X-Inertia: true` | answer with the JSON page object instead of the HTML shell |
| → request | `X-Inertia-Version` | the asset version the client holds; a mismatch on a **GET** forces a hard reload |
| → request | `X-Inertia-Partial-Component` | must equal the page's component, or the visit counts as a full one |
| → request | `X-Inertia-Partial-Data` / `-Partial-Except` | which props to resolve ([partial reloads](/d/spa/partial-reloads)) |
| → request | `X-Inertia-Reset` | return these merge props unmerged ([merging props](/d/spa/merging-props)) |
| → request | `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props` | cache keys the client still holds ([once props](/d/spa/once-props)) |
| → request | `X-Inertia-Error-Bag` | nest `props.errors` under a bag name ([validation](/d/spa/validation)) |
| → request | `X-Inertia-Infinite-Scroll-Merge-Intent` | `append` / `prepend` ([infinite scroll](/d/spa/infinite-scroll)) |
| → request | `Precognition: true` | dry-run the validation step only ([validation](/d/spa/validation)) |
| ← response | `200 text/html` | first load: the shell with the page object in `<script type="application/json" data-page="app">` |
| ← response | `200 application/json` + `X-Inertia: true` | an Inertia visit: the bare page object |
| ← response | `Vary: X-Inertia` | the same URL serves both |
| ← response | `303` | after a `PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` redirect, never `302` |
| ← response | `409` + `X-Inertia-Location` | asset-version mismatch, or an external `location()` |
| ← response | `409` + `X-Inertia-Redirect` | a redirect to a URL fragment |

## Two deployment modes

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="In-project">
    The SPA lives in `client/` inside the Blok project. Vite builds into
    `client/dist`, the Blok HTTP trigger serves it (`BLOK_STATIC_DIR`), and one
    origin answers everything. In dev, the Vite dev server proxies to Blok, so
    there is still one origin in the browser.
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Standalone">
    The SPA is its own deployable (a CDN, `:5173`, another host) and talks to
    Blok cross-origin. Blok sends CORS (`BLOK_CORS_ORIGIN`) that must **expose**
    the Inertia response headers, and the types travel through
    `blokctl gen app-types --out ../my-spa/src`.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Both are first-class; see [assets and versioning](/d/spa/assets-and-versioning)
for the wiring of each.

## Page = workflow, prop = step

`definePage()` declares the contract once, outside the workflow callback, so the
type is importable by the frontend and readable by codegen. `render()` emits
exactly **one** `page` control step, and the runner lowers it to one inner step
per prop (`<pageId>.<key>`) plus the serializer (`<pageId>.$render`).

That means props are ordinary steps: they run **in parallel**, each with its own
`retry`, `idempotencyKey` and `maxDuration`, each persisted to
`ctx.state["<pageId>.<key>"]`, and each free to be a node in another language.
Because they are concurrent, one prop can never read another's output — read the
request, or a middleware's output through [`shared()`](/d/spa/middleware).

| Mode | Full visit | Partial reload | Wrapper |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| regular | resolved | when named, or when nothing is named | — |
| `always` | resolved | always, exempt from `only`/`except` | `always(node)` |
| `optional` | never | only when named | `optional(node)` |
| `defer` | never (announced) | only when named / by group | `defer(node, { group, rescue })` |
| `merge` | resolved | resolved; labels ride partials only | `merge(node, { append, prepend, deep, matchOn })` |
| `once` | resolved unless the client holds it | same | `once(node, { as, until, fresh })` |
| `scroll` | resolved | resolved, with cursors | `scroll(node, { wrapper, pageName, metadata })` |

## What differs from Laravel

The adapter targets feature parity with
[`inertia-laravel`](https://github.com/inertiajs/inertia-laravel) **v3.3.4**
(released 2026-09-11), which is the version every row below was checked against.
Three things are deliberately different:

1. **No session store.** Laravel's flash rides the session; Blok has no session,
   so flash and error bags ride a **signed one-shot cookie**
   (`BLOK_FLASH_SECRET` is required). See [flash data](/d/spa/flash-data).
2. **Middleware is Blok's middleware.** There is no `HandleInertiaRequests`
   class. `inertia.shared`, `inertia.auth` and `inertia.csrf` are ordinary
   middleware **workflows** registered by name. See [middleware](/d/spa/middleware).
3. **Props are steps, not closures.** A prop is a node reference plus its
   inputs, resolved by the runner — which is why a prop can be Python, Go or
   Rust, and why per-prop retries exist at all.

## Packages

| Package | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `@blokjs/inertia` | the serializer node, `definePage()`, the middleware pack, shared data, routing, errors, SSR |
| `@blokjs/inertia-client` | typed `Pages`/`Routes`, `route()`, and the `blokInertia()` Vite plugin |
| `@blokjs/helpers` | the `@blokjs/flash`, `@blokjs/validate`, `@blokjs/csrf` and `@blokjs/throw` nodes |
| `@inertiajs/react` · `vue3` · `svelte` | the **stock** client, unforked |

# Getting started

Source: /d/spa/getting-started

Wire a Vite SPA to a Blok server by hand, render the first page, and run the two-terminal dev loop.

Counterpart: [Server-side setup](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/installation/server-side-setup)
and [client-side setup](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/installation/client-side-setup)
in the Inertia docs. Everything they say about `createInertiaApp` still holds —
only the server half is Blok's.

## 0. The one-liner

The scaffold writes everything on this page for you:

```bash
blokctl create spa my-app --framework react   # a standalone SPA project
blokctl add spa --framework vue               # a SPA inside an existing Blok project
blokctl create project --spa svelte           # both, in one command
```

Flags: `--framework react|vue|svelte` (Angular is refused — no Inertia adapter
exists), `--blok-url <url>` (default `http://localhost:4000`), `--pm`,
`--no-install`, `--ssr`. Add `--kit auth` for sessions, sign-in, sign-up,
password reset and a guarded page — see [Starter kit](/d/spa/starter-kit).

`add spa` refuses to run twice (it detects `client/`) and refuses outside a
Blok project. The five steps below are what it writes — read them to understand
the result, or to wire a client by hand.

## 1. Install

<CodeGroup>
```bash React
npm i @blokjs/inertia @blokjs/inertia-client @inertiajs/react @inertiajs/vite react react-dom
npm i -D vite @vitejs/plugin-react
```

```bash Vue
npm i @blokjs/inertia @blokjs/inertia-client @inertiajs/vue3 @inertiajs/vite vue
npm i -D vite @vitejs/plugin-vue
```

```bash Svelte
npm i @blokjs/inertia @blokjs/inertia-client @inertiajs/svelte @inertiajs/vite svelte
npm i -D vite @sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte
```
</CodeGroup>

Node 20.19+ is required (Vite's own floor). `@blokjs/inertia` registers its
nodes through `@blokjs/helpers` the moment it is installed — there is nothing to
wire into the node registry.

## 2. The client

The SPA lives in `client/` (in-project mode: Blok serves the built assets from
one origin).

```ts client/vite.config.ts
import { blokInertia } from "@blokjs/inertia-client/vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), blokInertia({ pages: { path: "src/pages" } })],
});
```

`blokInertia()` wraps `@inertiajs/vite`, so page resolution, lazy pages and the
SSR transform are upstream behaviour. On top it writes the four files the Blok
server reads — see [assets and versioning](/d/spa/assets-and-versioning).

```tsx client/src/main.tsx
import { createInertiaApp } from "@inertiajs/react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";

void createInertiaApp({
  setup({ el, App, props }) {
    if (el) createRoot(el).render(<App {...props} />);
  },
});
```

<Warning>
Do **not** hand-write `resolve: (name) => import(`./pages/${name}.tsx`)`. Vite
resolves a template-literal dynamic import only ONE directory deep, so a nested
page such as `Orders/Create` throws `Unknown variable dynamic import` in a
production build. With no `resolve`, `@inertiajs/vite` injects an
`import.meta.glob("./pages/**/*.tsx")` resolver that handles any depth; pass
`pages: { path, extension }` if your pages live somewhere other than
`src/pages`.
</Warning>

```tsx client/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx
interface Props {
  auth: { email: string };
  orders: { id: string; total: number }[];
}

export default function Dashboard({ auth, orders }: Props) {
  return (
    <main>
      <h1>{auth.email}</h1>
      <ul>
        {orders.map((order) => (
          <li key={order.id}>{order.total}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </main>
  );
}
```

## 3. The page workflow

A page is a workflow. The contract is declared **outside** the callback so the
frontend can `import type` it.

```ts src/workflows/dashboard.ts
import { defineNode, http, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { always, definePage, shared } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

export const currentUser = defineNode({
  name: "current-user",
  description: "The signed-in user, from the request headers.",
  input: z.object({ headers: z.record(z.string()).optional() }),
  output: z.object({ id: z.string(), email: z.string() }),
  execute: () => ({ id: "u-1", email: "ada@example.com" }),
});

const listOrders = defineNode({
  name: "list-orders",
  description: "This user's orders.",
  input: z.object({ userId: z.string() }),
  output: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string(), total: z.number() })),
  execute: (_ctx, input) => [{ id: `o-${input.userId}`, total: 120 }],
});

export const Dashboard = definePage("Dashboard", {
  auth: always(currentUser),
  orders: listOrders,
});

export default workflow(
  "dashboard",
  { version: "1.0.0", trigger: http.get("/dashboard") },
  (req) => {
    Dashboard.render(req, "page", "/dashboard", {
      auth: {},
      orders: { userId: shared(currentUser, "auth").id },
    });
  },
);
```

<Note>
`render(req, id, url, inputs, options?)` takes **node inputs per prop**, not
values: the runner decides per request which prop nodes actually run. `shared()`
is the typed read of a state slot the middleware filled in.
</Note>

## 4. Register the middleware

`inertia.shared` is an ordinary Blok middleware workflow. It fills `auth` and
reads the signed flash cookie; the `page` step folds the flash into the response
by itself.

```ts src/Workflows.ts
import { createAuthMiddleware, createSharedMiddleware } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { WorkflowRegistry } from "@blokjs/runner";
import dashboard, { currentUser } from "./workflows/dashboard";

export default {
  "inertia.shared": await createSharedMiddleware({ currentUser }),
  "inertia.auth": await createAuthMiddleware({ redirectTo: "/login" }),
  dashboard,
};

WorkflowRegistry.getInstance().setGlobalMiddleware(["inertia.shared"]);
```

Guard a route with `trigger: http.get("/orders", { middleware: ["inertia.auth"] })`.
Details in [middleware](/d/spa/middleware).

## 5. Environment

| Variable | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `BLOK_FLASH_SECRET` | **required** — signs the one-shot flash cookie (there is no session store) |
| `BLOK_STATIC_DIR` | `client/dist` — makes Blok serve the built SPA and read `ASSET_VERSION` |
| `BLOK_CORS_ORIGIN` | standalone mode only: the SPA's origin |

```bash
BLOK_FLASH_SECRET="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"
BLOK_STATIC_DIR=client/dist
```

## The dev loop

Two terminals:

```bash
# terminal 1 — the Blok server
BLOK_STATIC_DIR=client/dist blokctl dev

# terminal 2 — Vite
cd client && npx vite
```

Open the **Blok** URL (`http://localhost:4000`). The Vite plugin writes
`client/dist/.blok-vite.json` while its dev server runs, and the HTML shell
loads the entry and the HMR client straight from Vite — so edits hot-reload on
Blok's own origin. The **Vite** URL works too: everything it does not own is
proxied to `BLOK_URL` (default `http://localhost:4000`) with
`X-Inertia-Version: dev` attached, so a dev visit can never 409 on a stale
asset version.

<Note>
`BLOK_STATIC_DIR` matters in dev as well: it is where the server looks for
`.blok-vite.json`. Without it the shell has no `<script>` tag and the page is
blank — the server says so once, with the fix, in the log.
</Note>

For production: `vite build`, then start Blok with `BLOK_STATIC_DIR=client/dist`.
Blok serves `/assets/*` immutable and answers every other path from a workflow.

## Typing the client

Two paths, both real:

- **monorepo** — `import type { Dashboard }` and read
  `PageProps<typeof Dashboard>`;
- **separate repo** — `blokctl gen app-types --pages-only --out ../my-spa/src`
  writes `blok-pages.d.ts` and `blok-routes.ts`.

Both are spelled out in [pages and props](/d/spa/pages-and-props#typing-the-client)
and in the [`gen app-types`](/d/cli/gen) reference.

## Examples

Four runnable examples live in the repository:

| Example | What it shows |
| --- | --- |
| `examples/inertia-react` | in-project mode, a `runtime.python3` prop, defer/merge/once/scroll, a form with validation |
| `examples/inertia-vue` | the same server, a Vue 3 client |
| `examples/inertia-svelte` | the same server, a Svelte 5 client |
| `examples/inertia-standalone` | `backend/` + `frontend/` on two origins, CORS and `gen app-types --out` |

Each has a README, and `bun run e2e` runs its `runPage` suite.

# Pages and props

Source: /d/spa/pages-and-props

definePage, the seven prop modes, cross-runtime props, and the two ways the client gets its types.

Counterpart: [Pages](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/the-basics/pages) and
[Responses](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/the-basics/responses).

A page is declared **once**, outside the workflow callback. That placement is
the whole point: a contract declared inside the callback cannot leak its
inferred type to module scope, so the frontend would have nothing to import.

```ts src/pages/orders.ts
import { defineNode, http, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { always, defer, definePage, merge, once, optional, scroll } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

export const currentUser = defineNode({
  name: "current-user",
  description: "The signed-in user.",
  input: z.object({ headers: z.record(z.string()).optional() }),
  output: z.object({ id: z.string(), email: z.string() }),
  execute: () => ({ id: "u-1", email: "ada@example.com" }),
});

const listOrders = defineNode({
  name: "list-orders",
  description: "Orders for one user.",
  input: z.object({ userId: z.string() }),
  output: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string(), total: z.number() })),
  execute: (_ctx, input) => [{ id: `o-${input.userId}`, total: 120 }],
});

const loadFilters = defineNode({
  name: "load-filters",
  description: "Filter chips — only when the client asks.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ statuses: z.array(z.string()) }),
  execute: () => ({ statuses: ["open", "paid"] }),
});

const heavyStats = defineNode({
  name: "heavy-stats",
  description: "Expensive aggregates.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ revenue: z.number() }),
  execute: () => ({ revenue: 42_000 }),
});

const loadFeed = defineNode({
  name: "load-feed",
  description: "Activity feed page.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ data: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string() })) }),
  execute: () => ({ data: [{ id: "a-1" }] }),
});

const loadPlans = defineNode({
  name: "load-plans",
  description: "Pricing plans — rarely change.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string(), price: z.number() })),
  execute: () => [{ id: "pro", price: 20 }],
});

const listPosts = defineNode({
  name: "list-posts",
  description: "One page of posts.",
  input: z.object({ page: z.union([z.number(), z.string()]).optional() }),
  output: z.object({
    data: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string() })),
    pageName: z.string(),
    currentPage: z.number(),
    nextPage: z.number().nullable(),
    previousPage: z.number().nullable(),
  }),
  execute: () => ({
    data: [{ id: "p-1" }],
    pageName: "page",
    currentPage: 1,
    nextPage: 2,
    previousPage: null,
  }),
});

export const OrdersIndex = definePage("Orders/Index", {
  auth: always(currentUser),      // ignores every only/except filter
  orders: listOrders,             // regular
  filters: optional(loadFilters), // only when asked for by name
  stats: defer(heavyStats, { group: "dashboard", rescue: true }),
  feed: merge(loadFeed, { append: "data", matchOn: "id" }),
  plans: once(loadPlans, { until: "1h" }),
  posts: scroll(listPosts),
});

export default workflow(
  "orders",
  { version: "1.0.0", trigger: http.get("/orders") },
  (req) => {
    OrdersIndex.render(
      req,
      "page",
      "/orders",
      { orders: { userId: "u-1" }, posts: { page: req.query.page } },
      { version: "v1" },
    );
  },
);
```

## `render()`

```text
render(req, id, url, inputs, options?) -> Handle<RespondEnvelope>
```

| Argument | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `req` | the trigger entry handle (the workflow callback's argument) |
| `id` | the step id. Prop steps become `<id>.<propKey>`, the serializer `<id>.$render` |
| `url` | the page-object `url` — a literal or a handle |
| `inputs` | **node inputs per prop**, handles allowed. A prop whose node needs no input may be omitted |
| `options` | page-level knobs: `version`, `errors`, `flash`, `viewData`, `shell`, `head`, `rootId`, `encryptHistory`, `clearHistory`, `preserveFragment`, `exposeSharedPropKeys` |

It emits exactly one `page` control step. The runner lowers it to one inner step
per selected prop plus the serializer, resolves the selected props **in
parallel**, and persists each to `ctx.state["<id>.<key>"]`.

<Warning>
Because props run concurrently, **one prop can never read another's output**.
Read the request, or a middleware step's output through `shared()`.
</Warning>

## The seven modes

| Mode | Full visit | Partial reload | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| regular | resolved | when named, or when nothing is named | the default |
| `always(node)` | resolved | always | exempt from `only` **and** `except` |
| `optional(node)` | never | only when named | [partial reloads](/d/spa/partial-reloads) |
| `defer(node, opts)` | announced, not resolved | on the follow-up request | [deferred props](/d/spa/deferred-props) |
| `merge(node, opts)` | resolved | resolved + labelled | [merging props](/d/spa/merging-props) |
| `once(node, opts)` | resolved unless the client holds it | same | [once props](/d/spa/once-props) |
| `scroll(node, opts)` | resolved with cursors | resolved with cursors | [infinite scroll](/d/spa/infinite-scroll) |

`merge` and `scroll` describe what the **client** does with a value, so they
never take the resolution slot. Wrappers compose, and the innermost resolution
mode wins:

```ts src/compose.ts
import { defineNode } from "@blokjs/core";
import { defer, merge, once } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const loadResults = defineNode({
  name: "load-results",
  description: "Search results.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ data: z.array(z.string()) }),
  execute: () => ({ data: ["a"] }),
});

export const deferredAndMergeable = defer(merge(loadResults, { deep: true }), { group: "dashboard" });
export const rememberedAndMergeable = once(merge(loadResults, { append: "data" }));
```

### Per-prop reliability

A prop is a step, so the step knobs apply per prop in the JSON form
(`retry`, `idempotencyKey`, `idempotencyKeyTTL`, `maxDuration`):

```json
{
  "id": "page",
  "page": {
    "component": "Orders/Index",
    "props": {
      "stats": { "use": "heavy-stats", "mode": "defer", "group": "dashboard", "rescue": true, "maxDuration": 5000 }
    }
  }
}
```

A prop declared `rescue: true` that throws is omitted from `props`, listed in
`rescuedProps`, and logged — the run still succeeds. Without `rescue`, a throw
fails the workflow like any other step.

## Cross-runtime props

A prop is a node reference, so a prop can live in any runtime Blok speaks. Declare
the sidecar node with `runtimeNode<In, Out>(name, kind)` and use it like any other:

```ts src/python-prop.ts
import { http, runtimeNode, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { defer, definePage } from "@blokjs/inertia";

const stats = runtimeNode<{ since: string }, { revenue: number; orders: number }>(
  "dashboard-stats",
  "runtime.python3",
);

export const Dashboard = definePage("Dashboard", {
  stats: defer(stats, { group: "dashboard" }),
});

export default workflow(
  "dashboard",
  { version: "1.0.0", trigger: http.get("/dashboard") },
  (req) => {
    Dashboard.render(req, "page", "/dashboard", { stats: { since: "2026-01-01" } });
  },
);
```

The Python node is ordinary Blok — `runtimes/python3/nodes/dashboard_stats/node.py`
with a `@node("dashboard-stats", …)` function. Nothing about Inertia reaches it:
it gets inputs, it returns output, the runner persists the result and the
serializer ships it. `examples/inertia-react` has the full version.

<Note>
A `runtimeNode()` stub carries no Zod schema, so `blokctl gen app-types` types
that prop `unknown` and warns. Give the stub explicit `In`/`Out` type
parameters — that is what `PageProps` reads in the monorepo path.
</Note>

## Typing the client

### Path A — one repository

```tsx client/src/pages/Orders/Index.tsx
import type { PageProps } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import type { OrdersIndex } from "../../../../src/pages/orders";

export default function Index({ orders, stats }: PageProps<typeof OrdersIndex>) {
  return (
    <ul>
      {orders.map((order) => (
        <li key={order.id}>
          {order.total} {stats?.revenue}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  );
}
```

`optional` and `defer` keys are `T | undefined` — the client only receives them
on the visit that asked. Every other mode is present. `errors` is always there.

### Path B — separate repositories

```bash
blokctl gen app-types --pages-only --out ../my-spa/src
```

writes `blok-pages.d.ts` (augments `Pages`, `Routes` and Inertia's own
`InertiaConfig`) and `blok-routes.ts` (a `registerRoutes()` call). The client
then reads `PageProps<"Orders/Index">` from `@blokjs/inertia-client` with no
import from the server at all. Full reference: [`gen app-types`](/d/cli/gen).

## Reusable prop bundles

```ts src/bundles.ts
import { defineNode } from "@blokjs/core";
import { always, definePage, withProps } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const currentUser = defineNode({
  name: "current-user",
  description: "The signed-in user.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ id: z.string() }),
  execute: () => ({ id: "u-1" }),
});

const loadNav = defineNode({
  name: "load-nav",
  description: "Navigation items.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.array(z.string()),
  execute: () => ["orders"],
});

const loadStats = defineNode({
  name: "load-stats",
  description: "Home statistics.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ revenue: z.number() }),
  execute: () => ({ revenue: 1 }),
});

const dashboard = withProps({ auth: always(currentUser), nav: loadNav });

export const Home = definePage("Home", { ...dashboard, stats: loadStats });
```

`definePage()` throws if a component name is declared twice — the component name
is the page's identity, for `PageProps`, for codegen and for the registry.
`getPageRegistry()` returns every page declared in the process (component,
per-prop mode metadata, Zod output schema, source `file:line`), which is what
`blokctl gen` and [DevTools](/d/spa/devtools) read.

# Forms and redirects

Source: /d/spa/forms-and-redirects

useForm on the client, redirectBack on the server, the 303 rule, and where errors come from.

Counterparts: [Forms](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/the-basics/forms) and
[Redirects](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/the-basics/redirects).

The client half is stock Inertia — `useForm`, `<Form>`, `router.post()`. The
server half is one workflow that validates, writes, and **redirects back**.

```tsx client/src/pages/Orders/Create.tsx
import { useForm } from "@inertiajs/react";

export default function Create() {
  const form = useForm({ sku: "", qty: 1 });
  return (
    <form
      onSubmit={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        form.post("/orders");
      }}
    >
      <input value={form.data.sku} onChange={(e) => form.setData("sku", e.target.value)} />
      {form.errors.sku && <span>{form.errors.sku}</span>}
      <button type="submit" disabled={form.processing}>
        Save
      </button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

```ts src/workflows/orders-create.ts
import { branch, defineNode, eq, http, step, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { ValidateNode } from "@blokjs/helpers";
import { redirectBack } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const OrderSchema = z.object({
  sku: z.string().min(1, "Required."),
  qty: z.number().min(1, "Too few."),
});

const createOrder = defineNode({
  name: "create-order",
  description: "Persist an order and bounce back with a toast.",
  input: z.object({ order: z.unknown() }),
  output: z.object({ id: z.string() }),
  execute: () => ({ id: "o-1" }),
});

const bounceBack = defineNode({
  name: "bounce-back",
  description: "Redirect back with the validation errors.",
  input: z.object({ errors: z.record(z.unknown()) }),
  output: z.unknown(),
  execute: (ctx, input) =>
    redirectBack(ctx.request, { errors: input.errors, fallback: "/orders/new" }),
});

export default workflow(
  "orders-create",
  { version: "1.0.0", trigger: http.post("/orders") },
  (req) => {
    const checked = step("check", ValidateNode, { schema: OrderSchema, data: req.body });
    branch("route", eq(checked.ok, true), {
      then: () => {
        step("create", createOrder, { order: checked.data });
      },
      else: () => {
        step("reject", bounceBack, { errors: checked.errors });
      },
    });
  },
);
```

<Note>
`req.body` is `unknown` on the entry handle — an HTTP body is whatever the
client sent. Feeding it to a validation step needs no cast; **reading a field
off it** does:

```ts src/body-cast.ts
import type { Handle } from "@blokjs/core";

declare const req: { body: Handle<unknown> };

const body = req.body as Handle<{ sku: string; qty: number }>;
export const sku = body.sku;
```

The Zod schema on the validation step is what actually enforces the shape; the
cast only names it for the reads.
</Note>

## The 303 rule

A redirect answering a `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` must be a **303**, never a
302: a 302 makes the browser replay the write against the redirect target.
`redirectBack()` and `redirect()` apply the rule from the request method, and
the HTTP trigger runs a safety net — a `302` leaving the trigger on a non-GET
Inertia request is rewritten to `303`, so a middleware short-circuit or a rate
limiter cannot leak a replayable redirect.

## `redirectBack()` and `flash()`

```ts src/redirects.ts
import { back, flash, redirectBack } from "@blokjs/inertia";

const request = { headers: { referer: "/orders/new" }, method: "POST" };

export const withErrors = redirectBack(request, {
  errors: { sku: "Required." },
  bag: "createOrder",
  fallback: "/orders",
});

export const withToast = flash("toast", "Order created.").redirectBack(request);
export const alias = back(request, { fallback: "/" });
```

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `errors` | validation errors, persisted in the signed cookie |
| `bag` | error-bag name — defaults to the request's `X-Inertia-Error-Bag` |
| `flash` | arbitrary flash payload (`flash("toast", …)` is the chainable form). The toast helper the examples ship renders STRING values; an object needs a component of your own |
| `fallback` | where to go when the request carried no `Referer` |
| `preserveFragment` | keep the URL fragment across the bounce |
| `clearHistory` | ask the client to drop its encrypted history |

Everything it persists rides the **signed one-shot cookie**, because Blok has no
session — see [flash data](/d/spa/flash-data). `BLOK_FLASH_SECRET` is required.

## Where `errors` comes from

`props.errors` is always present (`{}` when there are none). Three sources, in
this order:

1. the `errors` option on `render()`,
2. the flash cookie the `inertia.shared` middleware read back after a bounce,
3. nothing — `{}`.

`withAllErrors: true` ships **every** message per field (`string[]`) instead of
the first (`string`); pass the same flag to `blokctl gen app-types` so the
generated types agree. Error bags nest the object one level deeper, which is
what lets two forms on one page keep their errors apart.

## Redirecting elsewhere

```ts src/elsewhere.ts
import { location, redirect } from "@blokjs/inertia";

export const toBilling = location("https://billing.example.com");   // 409 + X-Inertia-Location
export const toOrders = redirect("/orders", { method: "PUT" });      // 303
export const toSection = redirect("/orders#new");                    // 409 + X-Inertia-Redirect
```

# Middleware

Source: /d/spa/middleware

There is no HandleInertiaRequests — inertia.shared, inertia.auth and inertia.csrf are ordinary Blok middleware workflows.

Counterpart: [Authentication](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/security/authentication)
(Laravel's `HandleInertiaRequests` middleware class). Blok has no adapter-specific
middleware system: these are [ordinary middleware workflows](/d/reference/middleware),
registered by name, running on the parent `ctx` before the page workflow.

```ts src/Workflows.ts
import { defineNode } from "@blokjs/core";
import { createAuthMiddleware, createCsrfMiddleware, createSharedMiddleware } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { WorkflowRegistry } from "@blokjs/runner";
import { z } from "zod";

const currentUser = defineNode({
  name: "current-user",
  description: "Who is signed in, from the request headers.",
  input: z.object({ headers: z.record(z.string()).optional() }),
  output: z.object({ id: z.string().optional(), email: z.string().optional() }),
  execute: () => ({ id: "u-1", email: "ada@example.com" }),
});

export default {
  "inertia.shared": await createSharedMiddleware({ currentUser }),
  "inertia.auth": await createAuthMiddleware({ redirectTo: "/login" }),
  "inertia.csrf": await createCsrfMiddleware({ except: ["webhooks/*"] }),
};

WorkflowRegistry.getInstance().setGlobalMiddleware(["inertia.shared", "inertia.csrf"]);
```

Per route: `trigger: http.get("/orders", { middleware: ["inertia.auth"] })`.

| Workflow | Steps | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inertia.shared` | `auth`, `flash` | runs your `currentUser` node into `ctx.state.auth`, then verifies and clears the signed [flash cookie](/d/spa/flash-data) into `ctx.state.flash` |
| `inertia.auth` | `inertiaGuest`, `inertiaAuthGate`, `inertiaAuthRedirect` | when `auth.id` is missing, throws `302 Location: /login` — an Inertia visit follows a redirect, but has nothing to render from a bare 401 |
| `inertia.csrf` | `csrf` (ephemeral) | issues and verifies the [`XSRF-TOKEN` double submit](/d/spa/csrf) |
| `inertia.encryptHistory` | `encrypt-history` (ephemeral) | marks the request so every page in it encrypts its [history entry](/d/spa/history-encryption) |

<Warning>
**Reserved step ids: `auth` and `flash`.** Step ids are one flat namespace per
run, and middleware shares the page workflow's `ctx` — so a page step called
`auth` overwrites the signed-in user. `inertia.auth`'s own ids are prefixed
(`inertiaGuest`, `inertiaAuthGate`, `inertiaAuthRedirect`) for the same reason.
</Warning>

## Reading what the middleware left

`shared()` is the typed read of a state slot this workflow did not declare:

```ts src/read-auth.ts
import { defineNode, http, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { definePage, shared } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const currentUser = defineNode({
  name: "current-user",
  description: "Who is signed in.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ id: z.string(), email: z.string() }),
  execute: () => ({ id: "u-1", email: "ada@example.com" }),
});

const listOrders = defineNode({
  name: "list-orders",
  description: "Orders for one user.",
  input: z.object({ userId: z.string() }),
  output: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string() })),
  execute: () => [{ id: "o-1" }],
});

const OrdersPage = definePage("Orders/Index", { orders: listOrders });

export default workflow(
  "orders",
  { version: "1.0.0", trigger: http.get("/orders", { middleware: ["inertia.shared", "inertia.auth"] }) },
  (req) => {
    OrdersPage.render(req, "page", "/orders", {
      orders: { userId: shared(currentUser, "auth").id },
    });
  },
);
```

`shared(node, stepId)` is `makeHandle` with the node supplying the type — no
runtime magic, just a typed reference to `ctx.state[stepId]`.

## With the `page` step there is nothing to wire

The `page` control step reads the `flash` slot itself and folds it into the
serializer's inputs: `errors`, the error bag, page flash, `preserveFragment`,
`clearHistory`, and the clearing `Set-Cookie`. Anything passed through
`render()`'s options wins, and `errors` / `flash` **merge** with your keys on
top.

A hand-written serializer step wires those fields itself — see
[flash data](/d/spa/flash-data#without-the-page-step).

## Writing your own

An Inertia middleware is just a middleware. Anything that belongs on every page
(a tenant lookup, a locale, a feature-flag snapshot) can be either:

- a **middleware step**, when a prop's *inputs* need the value
  (`shared(node, "tenant")`), or
- a [shared-data registry](/d/spa/shared-data) entry, when the *page* needs it
  (`share("tenant", …)`).

```ts src/tenant-middleware.ts
import { defineNode, step, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { z } from "zod";

const resolveTenant = defineNode({
  name: "resolve-tenant",
  description: "Tenant for this request.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ id: z.string() }),
  execute: () => ({ id: "acme" }),
});

export const tenantMiddleware = workflow(
  "app.tenant",
  { version: "1.0.0", middleware: true },
  () => {
    step("tenant", resolveTenant, {});
  },
);
```

Register it under a name, add it to the global chain or a route's list, and read
it with `shared(resolveTenant, "tenant")`.

# Assets and versioning

Source: /d/spa/assets-and-versioning

The blokInertia() Vite plugin, ASSET_VERSION, the 409 reload, static serving, and CORS for standalone mode.

Counterpart: [Asset versioning](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/advanced/asset-versioning).
Laravel computes a version in `HandleInertiaRequests::version()`; Blok reads one
the Vite plugin wrote.

## The Vite plugin

```ts client/vite.config.ts
import { blokInertia } from "@blokjs/inertia-client/vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    react(),
    blokInertia({
      pages: { path: "src/pages", extension: [".tsx"] },
      proxy: { target: "http://localhost:4000" },
      ssr: { entry: "src/ssr.tsx" },
    }),
  ],
});
```

`blokInertia()` **wraps** `@inertiajs/vite`: page resolution, lazy pages, the
SSR transform and the HMR-backed dev SSR endpoint are all upstream behaviour,
and every `@inertiajs/vite` option is passed through. On top it writes into the
Vite `outDir` (`dist/` by default) — the handoff directory the Blok server
reads:

| File / value | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `dist/.blok-vite.json` | **what to load**: the entry, its stylesheets and its static imports, or the dev server's URL. See below |
| `dist/.blok-asset-version` | sha256 of `dist/.vite/manifest.json`, `"dev"` while the dev server runs. The serializer reads it on every render as the page object's `version` (a page's own `render(..., { version })` still wins), so a rebuild is announced without a restart |
| `import.meta.env.BLOK_ASSET_VERSION` | the same value, inlined into the bundle |
| `dist/pages.json` | `{ root, pages }` — the page components found on disk, for [`ensurePagesExist()`](/d/spa/routing#fail-the-boot-not-the-route) |
| `dist/.blok-ssr-url` + `import.meta.env.BLOK_SSR_URL` | where the server POSTs a page to be [rendered](/d/spa/ssr) |

`build.manifest` is forced on — the asset version is a hash of that manifest, so
turning it off is an error.

## Loading the bundle — Blok's `@vite`

Laravel's Blade template calls `@vite('resources/js/app.jsx')`. Blok's HTML
shell carries a marker, `<!--blok:assets-->`, and the serializer fills it from
`<BLOK_STATIC_DIR>/.blok-vite.json`. Vite hashes its filenames and, in dev,
serves the entry from its own origin, so the tags cannot be hard-coded.

After `vite build` the descriptor names the built files:

```json client/dist/.blok-vite.json
{
  "mode": "build",
  "entry": "assets/index-DucLcArp.js",
  "css": ["assets/index-DCQtc1cu.css"],
  "imports": [],
  "framework": "react"
}
```

and the shell emits, in order, a `<link rel="modulepreload">` per static import,
a `<link rel="stylesheet">` per stylesheet, and the module script:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/index-DCQtc1cu.css" />
<script type="module" src="/assets/index-DucLcArp.js"></script>
```

While `vite` is running the descriptor points at the dev server instead
(`{ "mode": "dev", "devUrl": "http://localhost:5173", "entry": "src/main.tsx" }`),
and the shell emits `/@vite/client`, the entry, and — for React — the
`@vitejs/plugin-react` refresh preamble, all as absolute URLs. That is what
makes the [dev loop](/d/spa/getting-started#the-dev-loop) work from the *Blok*
URL. The file is deleted when the dev server stops, so a later production boot
never points at a dead port.

<Note>
No descriptor means no `<script>` tag and a blank page, so the server logs one
warning naming the fix and still serves the HTML. The usual causes: the client
was never built, or `BLOK_STATIC_DIR` is not set.
</Note>

A custom `shell` without the `<!--blok:assets-->` marker is left exactly as
written — add the marker inside `<head>`, or pass your own tags as the
serializer's `assets` input.

## The 409 reload

When the client's `X-Inertia-Version` differs from the server's, a **GET**
answers `409` with `X-Inertia-Location: <url>` and the current version, and the
client does a hard visit — the new HTML pulls the new assets. It is never done
on another method: a replayed write would lose its body.

A pending [flash](/d/spa/flash-data) is re-signed onto that 409, so a toast
survives the forced reload.

<Note>
In dev the plugin's proxy attaches `X-Inertia-Version: dev` to every proxied
request, so a dev visit can never 409 on a version mismatch mid-edit.
</Note>

## Serving the build

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `BLOK_STATIC_DIR` | mounts the directory: `/assets/*` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, plus `favicon.ico` and `robots.txt` uncached. A miss under `/assets/*` is a hard `404`, never a fall-through to a workflow |
| `ASSET_VERSION` | fallback for the page `version` when `<staticDir>/.blok-asset-version` does not exist (the trigger also fills it from that file at boot, for its own log line) |

```bash
BLOK_STATIC_DIR=client/dist blokctl dev
```

With neither set, nothing static is mounted and `version` is `""` — "untracked",
which disables version checking entirely. Nothing in a workflow has to pass
`version`: the value comes from the build, in dev and in production alike.

## Standalone mode and CORS

With the proxy off (`proxy: false`) the SPA is served from its own origin and
talks to Blok cross-origin. Blok must then send CORS headers that cover
Inertia's protocol headers — a missing `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` entry is
invisible in the network tab but makes redirects and version mismatches
unreadable to the client.

```bash
BLOK_CORS_ORIGIN=https://app.example.com
```

Setting it turns on the CORS middleware with `credentials: true` and the full
Inertia / Precognition / DevTools header lists:

```http
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://app.example.com
Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
Access-Control-Allow-Headers: X-Inertia, X-Inertia-Version, X-Inertia-Partial-Data,
  X-Inertia-Partial-Component, X-Inertia-Partial-Except, X-Inertia-Reset,
  X-Inertia-Error-Bag, X-Inertia-Devtools-Request, X-Inertia-Devtools-Session,
  Precognition, Precognition-Validate-Only, X-XSRF-TOKEN
Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-Inertia, X-Inertia-Location, X-Inertia-Redirect,
  X-Inertia-Version, Precognition, Precognition-Success
```

<Warning>
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` must name the SPA origin explicitly. A value
containing `*` turns credentials **off** — and Inertia sends the session cookie
on every visit, so a wildcard origin silently logs everybody out.
</Warning>

In standalone mode the initial page comes from a JSON fetch rather than a
`data-page` attribute, through `createInertiaApp`'s `page` option, and the types
travel with `blokctl gen app-types --pages-only --out ../my-spa/src`.

  </Card>

# Server-side rendering

Source: /d/spa/ssr

The SSR wire contract, the entry file per framework, blokctl inertia start-ssr, and what happens when rendering fails.

Counterpart: [Server-side rendering](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/advanced/server-side-rendering).
Laravel runs `php artisan inertia:start-ssr`; Blok runs
`blokctl inertia start-ssr`, and speaks the same wire contract.

An initial, non-prefetch visit POSTs the page object to the SSR server and
injects the returned `head` and `body` into the [shell](/d/spa/title-and-meta).
Inertia visits (`X-Inertia: true`) are never server-rendered — there is no HTML
to produce.

## The entry file

The SSR entry is ordinary Inertia; `@inertiajs/vite` builds it and
`blokInertia()` records where it is.

```tsx client/src/ssr.tsx
import { type ResolvedComponent, createInertiaApp } from "@inertiajs/react";
import createServer from "@inertiajs/react/server";
import ReactDOMServer from "react-dom/server";

createServer((page) =>
  createInertiaApp({
    page,
    render: ReactDOMServer.renderToString,
    // A glob, never `import(`./pages/${name}.tsx`)`: Vite resolves a
    // template-literal import only one directory deep, so nested pages break.
    // (The SSR overload's types require `resolve`; the client entry may omit it.)
    resolve: (name: string) => {
      const pages = import.meta.glob<ResolvedComponent>("./pages/**/*.tsx", { import: "default" });
      return pages[`./pages/${name}.tsx`]();
    },
    setup: ({ App, props }) => <App {...props} />,
  }),
);
```

Vue uses `@inertiajs/vue3/server` with `createSSRApp` + `renderToString`, Svelte
`@inertiajs/svelte/server` — unchanged from the Inertia docs.

```ts client/vite.config.ssr.ts
import { blokInertia } from "@blokjs/inertia-client/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [blokInertia({ ssr: { entry: "src/ssr.tsx" } })],
});
```

## Running it

```bash
vite build && vite build --ssr           # client + ssr bundles
blokctl inertia start-ssr                # foreground; --port, --host, --runtime, --cluster
blokctl inertia check-ssr                # prints OK, or exits 1
blokctl inertia stop-ssr                 # POSTs /shutdown
```

| Flag | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `--runtime` | `BLOK_INERTIA_SSR_RUNTIME`, else `node` (`bun`, or an absolute path) |
| `--port` | `13714` |
| `--host` | `127.0.0.1` |
| `--cluster` | off — Inertia's clustered SSR server |

`start-ssr` runs in the foreground with the child's stdio inherited, so a
process manager supervises it the way it would any other server.

The bundle is discovered from `BLOK_INERTIA_SSR_BUNDLE`, else the first of
`client/dist-ssr/ssr.{js,mjs}`, `client/dist/server/ssr.{js,mjs}`,
`bootstrap/ssr/ssr.{js,mjs}`.

## Configuring the server half

```ts src/ssr-config.ts
import { configureSsr, disableSsr, withoutSsr } from "@blokjs/inertia";

configureSsr({ bundle: "client/dist-ssr/ssr.mjs", timeoutMs: 2_000, withoutSsr: ["admin/*"] });
withoutSsr(["admin/*", "dashboard"]);
disableSsr(() => process.env.NODE_ENV === "test");
```

| Where the endpoint comes from | Order |
| --- | --- |
| the page's own `ssr: { url }` input | first |
| `BLOK_SSR_URL` (empty string turns SSR **off**) | then |
| `<BLOK_STATIC_DIR ?? client/dist>/.blok-ssr-url`, written by the Vite plugin | then |
| `http://127.0.0.1:13714/render` | last |

| Variable | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BLOK_INERTIA_SSR_ENABLED` | on | `0`/`false`/`off`/`no` disables SSR |
| `BLOK_INERTIA_SSR_ENSURE_BUNDLE_EXISTS` | on | skip rendering when no bundle is on disk |
| `BLOK_INERTIA_SSR_THROW_ON_ERROR` | off | fail the request instead of falling back |
| `BLOK_INERTIA_SSR_TIMEOUT_MS` | `2000` | per-render timeout |

## When it fails

A failed render emits an `SsrRenderFailed` event (`ctx.publish`, plus any
`onSsrRenderFailed()` listener), logs **once per asset version and component**,
and **falls back to the client-rendered shell** — a broken SSR bundle degrades
to a working SPA, not to a 500. `configureSsr({ throwOnError: true })` makes
tests fail loudly instead.

<Note>
Text-fragment links (`#:~:text=`) require SSR, because the browser needs the
target text present in the initial HTML.
</Note>

# The protocol

Source: /d/spa/the-protocol

Every request header the adapter reads, every page-object field it emits, and every control response.

Counterpart: [The protocol](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/core-concepts/the-protocol).
Blok implements Inertia **v3** exactly; this page is the field-by-field
reference for `@blokjs/inertia`, the serializer node every page response passes
through.

The node takes a component name, already-resolved props and the request headers,
and returns a response envelope the HTTP trigger emits verbatim:

| Request | Response |
| --- | --- |
| no `X-Inertia` header | `200 text/html` — the shell, with the page object in `<script type="application/json" data-page="app">` |
| `X-Inertia: true` | `200 application/json` — the bare page object |

Both carry `Vary: X-Inertia`: one URL, two answers.

## Request headers

| Header | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `X-Inertia` | `true` selects the JSON page object over the HTML shell. |
| `X-Inertia-Version` | On a **GET**, a value different from the server's `version` produces the 409 conflict. Never on another method — a replayed write would lose its body. |
| `X-Inertia-Partial-Component` | Must equal the page's component, otherwise the request is treated as a full visit. |
| `X-Inertia-Partial-Data` | Comma-separated prop paths (dot notation) to keep. |
| `X-Inertia-Partial-Except` | Comma-separated prop paths to drop, applied **after** `Partial-Data`. |
| `X-Inertia-Reset` | Prop paths returned unmerged — stripped from `mergeProps` / `prependProps` / `deepMergeProps` (and from the `matchPropsOn` entries addressing them), with `scrollProps[<prop>].reset = true`. |
| `X-Inertia-Error-Bag` | Nests `props.errors` under that bag name. |
| `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props` | Cache keys the client still holds; those prop **nodes do not run**, though their `onceProps` entry is always echoed back. |
| `X-Inertia-Infinite-Scroll-Merge-Intent` | `append` / `prepend` — moves scroll props between `mergeProps` and `prependProps`. |
| `Purpose: prefetch` | A fragment redirect stays an ordinary redirect instead of becoming a 409, and SSR is skipped. |
| `Precognition` / `Precognition-Validate-Only` | Dry-run [validation](/d/spa/validation). |
| `X-XSRF-TOKEN` | The [CSRF](/d/spa/csrf) double-submit header. |

`errors` and every path in `alwaysProps` survive both partial-reload filters.

## Page-object fields

Always emitted: `component`, `props` (with `errors`, `{}` when there are none),
`url`, `version` (`""` when untracked). Everything else is **omitted** when it
does not apply — never `false`, never `[]`, never `{}`.

| Field | Emitted when |
| --- | --- |
| `encryptHistory` | the input is `true`, or the request/adapter default says so |
| `clearHistory` | the input is `true`, or the request was marked by `logoutResponse()` |
| `preserveFragment` | the input is `true` |
| `mergeProps` | this is a partial reload, non-empty after reset filtering |
| `prependProps` | this is a partial reload, non-empty after reset filtering |
| `deepMergeProps` | this is a partial reload, non-empty after reset filtering |
| `matchPropsOn` | this is a partial reload, non-empty (`"<propPath>.<keyField>"` entries) |
| `scrollProps` | non-empty — `{ <propKey>: { pageName, previousPage, nextPage, currentPage, reset } }`, keyed by the **prop** |
| `deferredProps` | non-empty **and** this is a full visit |
| `rescuedProps` | non-empty **and** this is a partial reload |
| `sharedProps` | non-empty and `exposeSharedPropKeys` is not `false` |
| `onceProps` | non-empty — `{ key: { prop, expiresAt } }`, `expiresAt` in epoch **milliseconds**, `null` when it never expires |
| `flash` | non-empty |

## Control responses

| Trigger | Response |
| --- | --- |
| version mismatch (GET only) | `409`, empty body, `X-Inertia-Location: <url>`, `X-Inertia-Version: <current>`, **no** `X-Inertia` header |
| `location(url)` | `409` + `X-Inertia-Location` — an external or hard visit |
| `redirect(url)` to a fragment | `409` + `X-Inertia-Redirect` (non-prefetch); an ordinary redirect otherwise |
| `redirect()` after `PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` | `303`, never `302` — a 302 makes the browser replay the write |
| `redirect(url, { preserveFragment: true })` | adds `X-Inertia-Preserve-Fragment: true` |

The HTTP trigger runs a safety net on top: a `302` leaving the trigger on a
non-GET request that carried `X-Inertia: true` is rewritten to `303`, so a
middleware short-circuit or a rate limiter cannot leak a replayable redirect.

```ts src/control.ts
import { location, redirect } from "@blokjs/inertia";

export const external = location("https://billing.example.com/portal");
export const bounce = redirect("/orders", { method: "PUT" });
```

## Prefetch

A request carrying `Purpose: prefetch` is served like any other visit, with two
differences: a fragment redirect is **not** promoted to a 409 (the client is not
navigating yet), and SSR is skipped. Once props the client already holds ride
along normally, so a prefetched page arrives complete.

## The shell

The default shell carries `<title data-inertia>` (v3 renamed the attribute from
`inertia`) and two markers:

| Marker | Replaced with |
| --- | --- |
| `<!--blok:head-->` | the `head` input — server-rendered `<Head>` tags |
| `<!--blok:app-->` | `<div id="app"></div>` plus the boot script |

`rootId` renames the root element and the script's `data-page` value. `viewData`
fills `{{key}}` placeholders and is **never** sent to the client. A custom
`shell` must contain `<!--blok:app-->`. See [title and meta](/d/spa/title-and-meta).

The page JSON is escaped for a `<script>` context — every `/` as `\/`, `<`
escaped, and the two JS line terminators — with **no** HTML-entity encoding,
because a browser does not decode entities inside a script element.
`JSON.parse(el.textContent)` round-trips it exactly.

<Warning>
Browsers store the page object in `history.state`, and Firefox hard-fails above
16 MiB — which surfaces as a Back button that simply does nothing. A page object
over **8 MiB** logs one warning per process and still ships. Move the bulk
behind [`defer()`](/d/spa/deferred-props) / `optional()`, or
[paginate](/d/spa/infinite-scroll) it.
</Warning>

## Writing the serializer step by hand

`definePage().render()` is the authoring surface, but the node is an ordinary
node and a JSON workflow can call it directly:

```json
{
  "id": "render",
  "use": "@blokjs/inertia",
  "inputs": {
    "component": "Users/Index",
    "props": { "users": { "$ref": { "step": "list-users", "path": ["users"] } } },
    "version": "v1"
  }
}
```

`headers`, `method` and `url` default to the live request, so a hand-written
step only needs `component` + `props`. A hand-written step must also wire the
flash itself — see [flash data](/d/spa/flash-data#without-the-page-step).

# Partial reloads

Source: /d/spa/partial-reloads

Which prop nodes the runner actually runs, per request — only, except, always and optional.

Counterpart: [Partial reloads](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/data-props/partial-reloads).

A partial reload is a visit that asks for a subset of a page's props. On Blok
that is not a filter over a computed response: the `page` control step decides
which prop **nodes run at all**, so a prop the client did not ask for costs
nothing.

```ts src/partial.ts
import { defineNode, http, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { always, definePage, optional } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const currentUser = defineNode({
  name: "current-user",
  description: "The signed-in user.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ id: z.string() }),
  execute: () => ({ id: "u-1" }),
});

const listUsers = defineNode({
  name: "list-users",
  description: "All users.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string() })),
  execute: () => [{ id: "u-1" }],
});

const loadFilters = defineNode({
  name: "load-filters",
  description: "Filter chips.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ statuses: z.array(z.string()) }),
  execute: () => ({ statuses: ["open"] }),
});

export const UsersIndex = definePage("Users/Index", {
  auth: always(currentUser),       // every visit, every filter
  users: listUsers,                // regular
  filters: optional(loadFilters),  // only when named
});

export default workflow(
  "users-index",
  { version: "1.0.0", trigger: http.get("/users") },
  (req) => {
    UsersIndex.render(req, "page", "/users", {});
  },
);
```

The client asks with the stock API — nothing Blok-specific:

```ts client/src/reload.ts
import { router } from "@inertiajs/core";

router.reload({ only: ["users"] });
router.reload({ except: ["users"] });
```

## Resolution table

| Visit | Runs | Does not run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full visit (no `X-Inertia-Partial-Component`, or one naming a different component) | `regular`, `always`, `merge`, `scroll`, and `once` unless the client still holds it | `optional`, `defer` |
| Partial reload with `X-Inertia-Partial-Data` | the named props (a dot path selects by its **root** segment) plus `always` — naming a `once` prop always resolves it | everything else |
| Partial reload without `X-Inertia-Partial-Data` | `regular`, `merge`, `scroll`, and `once` unless the client holds it, minus any `X-Inertia-Partial-Except`; `always` is exempt | `optional`, `defer` |

Two rules worth spelling out:

- **`always` beats both filters.** An `only` that does not name it still resolves
  it; an `except` that does name it still resolves it. Use it for the props a
  layout cannot render without (`auth`, feature flags).
- **The partial component must match.** If `X-Inertia-Partial-Component` names a
  different component, the request is a full visit — which is what makes a
  redirect to another page safe.

`errors` and every `always` path also survive the filters in the **serializer**,
so a validation error can never be filtered out of a partial response.

## Dot paths

`only: ["user.name"]` selects the prop by its root segment (`user`), resolves
that node, and the serializer narrows the value to the named path. The same
notation drives `except`.

## Testing it

`runPage` performs a **real second run** with the partial-reload headers, so a
test can assert that a node did not execute:

```ts src/partial.test.ts
import { runPage } from "@blokjs/core/testing";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import usersIndex from "./partial";

it("does not resolve optional props on a full visit", async () => {
  const page = await runPage(usersIndex);
  page.assert().component("Users/Index").has("users").missing("filters").etc();

  const reloaded = await page.reloadOnly("filters");
  expect(reloaded.props.filters).toBeDefined();
  expect(reloaded.run.step("page.users")?.executed).toBe(false);
});
```

# Deferred props

Source: /d/spa/deferred-props

Announce the expensive props on the first visit, let the client fetch them immediately after — with groups and rescue.

Counterpart: [Deferred props](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/data-props/deferred-props).
Laravel writes `Inertia::defer(fn () => …)`; Blok wraps the prop's **node**.

```ts src/deferred.ts
import { defineNode, http, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { defer, definePage } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const heavyStats = defineNode({
  name: "heavy-stats",
  description: "A slow aggregate query.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ revenue: z.number() }),
  execute: () => ({ revenue: 42_000 }),
});

const recentActivity = defineNode({
  name: "recent-activity",
  description: "Recent activity, also slow.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string() })),
  execute: () => [{ id: "a-1" }],
});

export const Dashboard = definePage("Dashboard", {
  stats: defer(heavyStats, { group: "dashboard" }),
  activity: defer(recentActivity, { group: "dashboard", rescue: true }),
});

export default workflow(
  "dashboard",
  { version: "1.0.0", trigger: http.get("/dashboard") },
  (req) => {
    Dashboard.render(req, "page", "/dashboard", {});
  },
);
```

The first visit carries **no** `stats`/`activity` value and instead announces:

```json
{ "deferredProps": { "dashboard": ["stats", "activity"] } }
```

The client then issues one partial reload per group. On the client side nothing
changes from the Inertia docs — `<Deferred data="stats" fallback={…}>` (React),
`<Deferred>` (Vue), `{#await}`-style usage in Svelte.

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `group` | props sharing a group are fetched in **one** follow-up request. Without it, each prop gets its own group (its key). |
| `rescue` | a throw omits the prop and lists it in `rescuedProps` instead of failing the run — it is logged, and the page still renders. |

<Note>
`deferredProps` is emitted on **full visits only**, and `rescuedProps` on
**partial reloads only** — that asymmetry is the protocol's, not Blok's.
</Note>

## Deferred *and* merged

`defer()` decides **when** a prop resolves; `merge()` decides what the client
does with it. They compose, innermost resolution mode winning:

```ts src/deferred-merge.ts
import { defineNode } from "@blokjs/core";
import { defer, merge } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const loadResults = defineNode({
  name: "load-results",
  description: "Search results.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ data: z.array(z.string()) }),
  execute: () => ({ data: ["a"] }),
});

export const results = defer(merge(loadResults, { deep: true }), { group: "search" });
```

A full visit announces it in `deferredProps` and carries **no** `scrollProps` or
merge labels; the follow-up partial carries both.

## Testing

```ts src/deferred.test.ts
import { runPage } from "@blokjs/core/testing";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import dashboard from "./deferred";

it("announces the group and resolves it on the follow-up", async () => {
  const page = await runPage(dashboard);
  expect(page.deferredProps).toEqual({ dashboard: ["stats", "activity"] });
  expect(page.run.step("page.stats")?.executed).toBe(false);

  await page.loadDeferredProps("dashboard", (p) => p.has("stats").has("activity").etc());
});
```

# Merging props

Source: /d/spa/merging-props

Append, prepend, deep-merge and match-on — the labels that tell the client to grow a prop instead of replacing it.

Counterpart: [Merging props](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/data-props/merging-props).
Laravel writes `Inertia::merge()` / `->deepMerge()` / `->matchOn()`; Blok wraps
the node with `merge()`.

`merge()` never changes **when** a prop resolves — only what the client does
with the value. The labels ride **partial reloads only**: a full visit replaces
props wholesale, so it carries none of `mergeProps`, `prependProps`,
`deepMergeProps` or `matchPropsOn`.

```ts src/merging.ts
import { defineNode, http, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { definePage, merge } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const loadUsers = defineNode({
  name: "load-users",
  description: "One page of users.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ data: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string() })) }),
  execute: () => ({ data: [{ id: "u-1" }] }),
});

export const appended = merge(loadUsers);                              // mergeProps: ["users"]
export const prepended = merge(loadUsers, { prepend: true });          // prependProps: ["users"]
export const nested = merge(loadUsers, { append: "data" });            // mergeProps: ["users.data"]
export const matched = merge(loadUsers, { append: "data", matchOn: "id" });
export const deep = merge(loadUsers, { deep: true, matchOn: "data.id" });
export const both = merge(loadUsers, { append: "data", prepend: "announcements" });
export const perPath = merge(loadUsers, { append: { "users.data": "id", messages: "uuid" } });

export const UsersFeed = definePage("Users/Feed", { users: nested });

export default workflow(
  "users-feed",
  { version: "1.0.0", trigger: http.get("/users") },
  (req) => {
    UsersFeed.render(req, "page", "/users", {});
  },
);
```

| Option | Type | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `append` | `true` \| `"data"` \| `string[]` \| `Record<string, string>` | what the client appends to. Default: the whole prop |
| `prepend` | same | what the client prepends to |
| `deep` | `boolean \| string` | deep-merge the whole prop, or one sub-path |
| `matchOn` | `string` | item field used to match and **replace** rows instead of appending |

A `matchPropsOn` entry is `"<mergePath>.<field>"` — the client splits on the
**last** dot, matches the head against the merge path, and replaces items whose
field matches. The map form (`append: { "users.data": "id" }`) gives each path
its own field; `matchOn` applies one field to every path the prop labels.

## Resetting

`X-Inertia-Reset: users` still **resolves** the prop — the client wants a fresh
copy — but returns it without labels, so it replaces rather than merges. The
stock client sends it for you:

```ts client/src/reset.ts
import { router } from "@inertiajs/core";

router.reload({ only: ["users"], reset: ["users"] });
```

Client-side prop helpers (`router.replaceProp`, `appendToProp`,
`prependToProp`) need nothing from the server.

## Testing

```ts src/merging.test.ts
import { runPage } from "@blokjs/core/testing";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import feed from "./merging";

it("labels the merge path on a partial reload only", async () => {
  const full = await runPage(feed);
  expect(full.mergeProps).toEqual([]);

  const partial = await full.reloadOnly("users");
  expect(partial.mergeProps).toEqual(["users.data"]);
});
```

# Once props

Source: /d/spa/once-props

Values the client remembers, so the prop's node never runs again — with keys, expiry and the sign-out pattern.

Counterpart: [Once props](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/data-props/once-props).
Laravel writes `Inertia::once(fn () => …)->until(…)->as(…)`; Blok wraps the node
with `once()`.

`once()` is the one mode that changes **resolution**: as soon as the client
holds the value it sends the cache key in `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props`, and the
prop's node is **not run at all** — only its `onceProps` entry comes back, or
the client would drop its cached copy.

```ts src/once.ts
import { defineNode, http, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { definePage, once } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const loadPlans = defineNode({
  name: "load-plans",
  description: "Pricing plans — they rarely change.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string(), price: z.number() })),
  execute: () => [{ id: "pro", price: 20 }],
});

export const Pricing = definePage("Pricing", {
  plans: once(loadPlans, { until: "1h" }),
});

export default workflow(
  "pricing",
  { version: "1.0.0", trigger: http.get("/pricing") },
  (req) => {
    Pricing.render(req, "page", "/pricing", {});
  },
);
```

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `as: "roles"` | the cache key, so two pages can share one remembered value under different prop names. Defaults to the prop key. |
| `until` | `"1h"` / `"500ms"` (a duration from now), a number of **seconds**, or an absolute date (`Date`, or anything `Date.parse` accepts). Emitted as `expiresAt` in epoch milliseconds; a deadline already in the past resolves again despite the header. |
| `fresh: true` | resolve and resend even when the client says it still holds the value. |

<Note>
`fresh` is a boolean, not a callback: prop metadata is workflow **config**,
JSON-cloned at boot, so a function would silently vanish. Decide per request
from the client (`router.reload({ only: ["plans"] })` always resolves) or from
inside the prop's own node.
</Note>

Explicit always wins: naming a once prop in `only` resolves it whatever the
header says. Prefetch requests carry the remembered entries like any other
request, so a prefetched page arrives with its once props already filled in.

## Sign-out: overwrite, do not forget

The documented auth pattern is to remember the user while signed in and
**overwrite** the remembered copy with `null` on sign-out — a plain prop of the
same key replaces whatever the client cached.

```ts src/auth-once.ts
import { defineNode } from "@blokjs/core";
import { definePage, once } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const currentUser = defineNode({
  name: "current-user",
  description: "The signed-in user, or null.",
  input: z.object({}),
  output: z.object({ id: z.string() }).nullable(),
  execute: () => ({ id: "u-1" }),
});

export const Layout = definePage("App/Layout", { auth: once(currentUser, { as: "auth" }) });
```

## Shared once props

The [shared-data registry](/d/spa/shared-data) has the same mode:

```ts src/shared-once.ts
import { shareOnce } from "@blokjs/inertia";

shareOnce("countries", async () => [{ code: "PT" }], { until: "1d" });
```

## Composing

`once(merge(node, { append: "data" }))` is remembered **and** mergeable — the
metadata modes contribute labels without taking the resolution slot.

# Infinite scroll

Source: /d/spa/infinite-scroll

scroll() props, the cursor metadata the client needs, and the paginate / cursorPaginate helpers.

Counterpart: [Infinite scroll](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/data-props/infinite-scroll).
Laravel writes `Inertia::scroll($users->paginate())`; Blok wraps the node with
`scroll()` and ships two pure pagination helpers.

`scroll()` is [`merge()`](/d/spa/merging-props) with a cursor. The prop resolves
like a regular one; the client's `<InfiniteScroll data="posts">` grows the item
array and replaces the cursors around it.

```ts src/feed.ts
import { defineNode, http, workflow } from "@blokjs/core";
import { definePage, paginate, paginatedSchema, scroll } from "@blokjs/inertia";
import { z } from "zod";

const Post = z.object({ id: z.string(), title: z.string() });

const listPosts = defineNode({
  name: "list-posts",
  description: "One page of posts.",
  input: z.object({ page: z.string().optional() }),
  output: paginatedSchema(Post),
  execute: (_ctx, input) => {
    const rows = [{ id: "p-1", title: "Hello" }];
    return paginate(rows, { page: Number(input.page ?? 1), perPage: 10 });
  },
});

export const Feed = definePage("Feed/Index", { posts: scroll(listPosts) });

export default workflow(
  "feed",
  { version: "1.0.0", trigger: http.get("/feed") },
  (req) => {
    Feed.render(req, "page", "/feed", { posts: { page: req.query.page } });
  },
);
```

| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `wrapper` | the sub-path holding the items — the one the client **grows**. Default `"data"`; `""` grows the whole prop. Only this path is labelled, so the cursors beside it are replaced. |
| `pageName` | the query parameter the client bumps. Overrides the resolved metadata's own — two scroll props on one page need distinct names (`?users=2&orders=3`). |
| `metadata` | `(output) => ScrollMetadata`, for an output that does not already carry the four cursor fields. |

<Warning>
The `scrollProps` entry is read from the **resolved output**, not from the
declaration, so every response re-emits a fresh cursor. An output that satisfies
neither `ScrollMetadata` (`pageName`, `previousPage`, `nextPage`, `currentPage`)
nor a `metadata` resolver **fails the request** — a feed that can never load the
next page is worse than a loud error.
</Warning>

## The pagination helpers

Pure functions; they hold no database opinion.

```ts src/paginate.ts
import { cursorPaginate, paginate } from "@blokjs/inertia";

const rows = [{ id: "1" }, { id: "2" }, { id: "3" }];

export const sliced = paginate(rows, { page: 1, perPage: 2 });          // rows = the WHOLE collection
export const trusted = paginate(rows, { page: 1, perPage: 2, total: 9 }); // rows = already one page
export const cursored = cursorPaginate(rows, { cursor: "abc", next: "def", prev: null });
```

`paginatedSchema(item)` and `cursorPaginatedSchema(item)` are their Zod forms,
for a node's `output`.

## What goes on the wire

| Request | Response |
| --- | --- |
| full visit | `props.posts`, `scrollProps.posts`, **no** merge label |
| partial + `X-Inertia-Infinite-Scroll-Merge-Intent: append` | `mergeProps: ["posts.data"]` |
| …`: prepend` | `prependProps: ["posts.data"]` |
| partial + `X-Inertia-Reset: posts` | `scrollProps.posts.reset = true`, no label |
| `defer(scroll(…))`, full visit | `deferredProps`, **no** `scrollProps`; both arrive on the deferred partial |

For a scroll prop, naming the prop (`posts`) or its wrapper path (`posts.data`)
in `X-Inertia-Reset` means the same thing.

# Shared data

Source: /d/spa/shared-data

share() and shareOnce() — values every page gets, resolved lazily, announced to the client for instant visits.

Counterpart: [Shared data](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/data-props/shared-data).
Laravel shares from `HandleInertiaRequests::share()`; Blok has a registry you
fill once at boot, and — for values a **prop** needs — the `inertia.shared`
middleware.

```ts src/bootstrap.ts
import { share, shareOnce } from "@blokjs/inertia";

share("appName", "Blok");                                    // static
share("auth", (req: unknown) => ({ user: userFrom(req) })); // LAZY: per request
share("flags", () => ({ beta: true }), { always: true });    // survives every partial filter
shareOnce("countries", async () => [{ code: "PT" }], { until: "1d" });

function userFrom(_req: unknown): { email: string } | null {
  return { email: "ada@example.com" };
}
```

Import that module once, before the workflows.

Shared values are merged **under** the page's own props — a page prop of the
same name wins, and the shared value is then never resolved at all — and their
top-level keys ride the page object as `sharedProps`, so
[instant visits](https://inertiajs.com/docs/v3/the-basics/instant-visits) can
carry them to the next page before the server answers. `exposeSharedPropKeys:
false` on a page hides the key list; the values still ship.

## Selection

Shared keys follow the same table as declared props:

| Request | `regular` | `always: true` | `shareOnce` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| full visit | resolved | resolved | resolved unless `X-Inertia-Except-Once-Props` names it |
| partial with `only` | only when named | resolved | only when named |
| partial without `only` | resolved | resolved | not resolved |
| `except` names it | not resolved | resolved | not resolved |

A lazy value is called with `ctx.request`, **at most once per request**, and
only when the key is actually selected — so `share("auth", expensive)` costs
nothing on a partial reload that asked for something else.

A prop resolver that needs another shared value reads it from the same
per-request cache:

```ts src/read-shared.ts
import { getShared } from "@blokjs/inertia";

export async function tenantOf(ctx: unknown): Promise<{ id: string }> {
  return await getShared<{ id: string }>("tenant", { id: "public" }, ctx);
}
```

<Warning>
**Namespace your shared data.** `share("auth", { user })`, not
`share("user", …)`: keys are top-level props and a page prop of the same name
silently wins. A key containing a dot is rejected for that reason.
</Warning>

## Registry or middleware?

Both exist, and they answer different questions.

| | `share()` registry | `inertia.shared` middleware |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resolved by | the serializer, on every response | two real steps, before the workflow |
| Reaches | the **client**, as a prop | `ctx.state`, so a prop's **inputs** can read it |
| Read with | `usePage().props.auth` | `shared(currentUser, "auth")` |
| Also does | — | verifies and clears the [flash cookie](/d/spa/flash-data) |

Use the middleware when a prop needs the value; use the registry when the page
does. Registry values reach a `page` step, a hand-written `step("render", …)`
and [`inertia.page()`](/d/spa/routing) alike — including
[error pages](/d/spa/error-handling), which render outside the middleware chain.

## Typing shared props on the client

Shared props are part of `PageProps` through Inertia's own config interface:

```ts client/src/inertia.d.ts
import "@inertiajs/core";

declare module "@inertiajs/core" {
  interface InertiaConfig {
    sharedPageProps: { auth: { user: { email: string } | null }; appName: string };
  }
}
```

`blokctl gen app-types` writes that block for you — see [`gen app-types`](/d/cli/gen).
